Restore accepts completion rows without reconciling them against current curriculum evidence.

evidence: V2Entities.kt and V2BackupFormat.kt completion models lack digest; LocalStore.kt readV2Learner maps rows to completedUnitNumbers; V2ProgressRules.kt unitState trusts the set. referencesResolve does not check v2 completion evidence. Static trace; full restore regression not run.

acceptance_test: Complete Unit 6, change its governed content/key, reload/restore: old attempts must not be current evidence and Unit 7 must not unlock solely from old Unit 6 row. Restore a hash-correct backup claiming completion with no supporting evidence and assert rejection or explicit unverified state.

evidence: All 30 ADVANCEMENT records independently inventoried: requireDueReview=true only in Unit 2. V2GovernedIdentity.kt practiceQueue and V2ProgressRules.kt gate trace.
proposed_correction: Define bounded versioned cumulative-review obligations and governed completion, using taught objectives; do not create another vocabulary SRS.
acceptance_test: Given due cumulative review and otherwise complete current work, advancement must remain blocked; complete the assigned multi-objective review and re-evaluate successfully. Never select untaught objectives.

observed_behavior: Foundation assessment is printed-letter/print-pair recognition. u1-st-decoding explicitly introduces no words; marked example words/model audio/handwriting assets are absent. Unit 2 has five repeated print-recognition checks and book-directed reading. Listening and Pronunciation labs explicitly cannot run.

evidence: Unit 1/2 packet objectives, teaching, five Unit 2 items; practiceOffers marks audio/handwriting absent. Private reference Lesson 1 sections 1.1-1.2 printed p1 (PDF13), sampled only. No claim of full book alignment.
proposed_correction: Research/admit bounded licensed foundation assets and checks, preserve truthful unavailable states until admitted; do not substitute arbitrary catalog audio.

observed_behavior: The objective is nominative role, but its choices select sentence translations. Recognizing husband/train vocabulary can pass without identifying the subject or nominative function; guided and first independent check are identical.
expected_behavior: Independent checks must test the named case role rather than only recognize a whole-sentence gloss.
evidence: Unit 4 packet objective and all three items. Cornell primary grammar confirms subject as principal nominative function (https://russian.cornell.edu/grammar/html/gr01_b_2_b.htm), retrieved 2026-10-12.
proposed_correction: Retain valid translations as examples and add a licensed/bound case-role contrast with a new independent application.
acceptance_test: A learner who knows the English gloss but chooses a different case role must fail the role check; a distinct taught subject-function application must be scored correctly.

observed_behavior: All six question-word cues visibly equal their keyed answer. The lesson renderer shows the Russian answer before a question asking which Russian word expresses the English purpose.
expected_behavior: Recognition checks should require selecting from the English purpose without printing the target answer as the cue.
evidence: All six packet promptLetter==answer comparisons independently reproduced; V2SessionScreen prints promptLetter.
proposed_correction: Remove the redundant Russian answer cue or use a contextual question that tests its function; update bound evidence and review digests.
acceptance_test: Assert the pre-answer screen does not disclose the keyed word; use a distinct independently bound question-purpose check and verify correct/wrong scoring.

observed_behavior: The learner is asked which flag the admitted row records, with options 1/0 and feedback repeating that flag. This is database-field recall rather than language use or a learner-facing grammatical explanation.
expected_behavior: Use explained declinable/indeclinable distinctions or contextual unchanged-form checks.
evidence: Unit 5 packet questions, feedback and obj-u5-indeclinable title.
proposed_correction: Keep the original database flag as provenance metadata; teach and assess the grammatical distinction in ordinary learner-facing language.
acceptance_test: A novice can explain the answer from taught morphology without seeing or knowing a source CSV flag; wrong answers expose a specific explanation.

observed_behavior: Several options end with the incomplete clause “we use the word” without naming it. Other options say “It is followed” without supplying the referent. These source fragments are presented as rules, and feedback repeats them.
expected_behavior: Rule choices must be complete, self-contained and explain the case/construction relevant to the cue.
evidence: Unit 8 availability and Unit 10 possession/absence packet item fields; exact affected IDs are listed in ITEM_ASSESSMENT_AUDIT.csv.
proposed_correction: Independently phrase complete bounded explanations and bind them as pending synthesis; preserve original source records separately.
acceptance_test: Every option has a complete proposition and explicit referent. A wrong response explains the required construction/case, not a cut-off source sentence.

observed_behavior: 135 item feedback blocks ask whether the answer shows the requested label/contrast and then repeat the key. They do not state the linguistic reason. Optional labs also omit lesson remediation/reference links.
expected_behavior: Explain the relevant ending, construction, subject, meaning or contrast; expose a directly relevant explanation after mistakes.
evidence: Literal phrase inventory independently counted 135 records. Representative u6-g-third-0, u9-i-quantity-1, u11-i-past-read-1. UI lab feedback displays only item.feedback.
proposed_correction: Rewrite feedback in bounded groups from retained sources and provide a remediation/reference route in labs; verify each competing option.
acceptance_test: For each affected item, a wrong answer yields an explanatory reason and reachable teaching/reference. A test asserting only key presence must not count as semantic validation.

observed_behavior: The past reading form is paired with keyed “in the present” because the question asks for the other time. The latest teaching explicitly coaches this reversal. The key follows the literal prompt; it is not an incorrect translation, but this item rewards complement-label selection rather than interpreting the displayed form.
expected_behavior: Use a distinct contextually supported active-time application to assess time; avoid training reversal as proof of form comprehension.
evidence: Unit 29 item and u29-st-teach-active-2; retained grammar capability contains past/present pair.
proposed_correction: Replace the reversal with a new admitted application or retain it as unscored metalinguistic practice outside the time gate.
acceptance_test: A displayed past form must not obtain time-comprehension credit solely by choosing the opposite label. Test a distinct governed form/context with explanatory feedback.

observed_behavior: The objective is deliberately narrowed to choosing glosses. The guided long form and independent short form both select “new”; the other independent item selects “beige” for an invariant colour term. None tests short versus long form, agreement or predicate function, although the source capability is short-form-adjective.
expected_behavior: Do not treat vocabulary glosses as sufficient demonstration of the required short-adjective grammar scope.
evidence: Unit 29 objective, three items, capability and new teaching. Private Lesson 29 heading and sections 29.1-29.2 sampled at printed p355/PDF367; detailed short-adjective book section was not inspected.
proposed_correction: Preserve correct glosses as vocabulary; add a licensed/bound grammatical contrast and independent application; keep broader coverage pending.
acceptance_test: A learner who recognizes “new” but cannot distinguish long/short form or taught predicate function cannot pass the short-form grammar check. Inspect every answer/distractor for the new context.

observed_behavior: The independent punctuation cue is a grammatical category phrase, not a sentence or participial construction. The answer is a source connective meaning “except in those cases”. Without a described word, phrase position or full construction, it cannot demonstrate punctuation application.
expected_behavior: Provide a complete taught construction and ask for its punctuation treatment, including the exception where applicable.
evidence: Unit 29 item and cap-obj-u29-punctuation exact source span independently read. The new instruction teaches the exception label but supplies no assessed contextual punctuation decision here.
proposed_correction: Use an admitted licensed example/application; keep the connective as source prose rather than an answer pretending to classify punctuation.
acceptance_test: A full exception construction requires a specific comma decision; the learner must not be able to pass by recalling the source connective. Verify default, exception and end-of-sentence boundary separately.

observed_behavior: The letter-name check keys an English comparison word from the same table row; the abbreviation check keys the English heading above the examples. These keys fit the source-layout prompts, but do not ask the learner to name a Russian letter or interpret/use the abbreviation. New teaching explicitly coaches these source positions.
expected_behavior: Treat row/heading recall as limited reference literacy; required letter-name/abbreviation scope needs a distinct language check.
evidence: Unit 30 items, objectives and latest teaching. All source-layout wording is retained; no wrong-key claim is made.
proposed_correction: Keep limited examples only if honestly labelled non-gating; add independently bound name and contextual abbreviation checks inside authorized source boundaries.
acceptance_test: Show a Russian letter and require its taught name, without English table-row clues. Show an admitted abbreviation in context and test its meaning/treatment; heading recall alone must not satisfy the language objective.

observed_behavior: The only directionality label check is guided. The four independent checks ask two lexical meanings and two prefixed-sentence readings; none contrasts unidirectional/multidirectional selection, although the objective names directionality and a source capability clears it.
expected_behavior: Require an independent taught directionality application before treating directionality as demonstrated.
evidence: Unit 20 objective, all five assessment items and readiness report listing five resolved capabilities. Source taxonomy is not an independent learner demonstration.
proposed_correction: Add a bounded licensed directional contrast/application, avoiding aspect/directionality conflation; reassess claimed coverage.
acceptance_test: After guided directionality practice, a distinct contextual directional question must be required and scored from a reviewed key. A vocabulary-only pass cannot demonstrate directionality.

observed_behavior: Eleven same-unit groups reuse the exact question tuple in guided and independent roles. Unit 17 repeats its clock-question tuple three times; Unit 28 repeats each timing question from guided practice as an independent check. This permits answer-memory rather than transfer. Distinct-signature advancement already deduplicates the tuple; no inflated distinct-count claim is made.

acceptance_test: Assert a required independent application differs in meaningful governed context/cue from the guided set, and that merely replaying the guided tuple cannot substitute for it.

observed_behavior: The Unit 21–25 notice says completion over a period is not prepared and later says the bounded task is implemented. The Unit 26–30 notice mixes unprepared participle-stress/dictionary wording with implemented bounded tasks. These retained present-tense gap statements confuse actual availability and broader coverage limits.

proposed_correction: Replace stale learner-facing sentences with precise current bounded availability and separate remaining-scope statements; retain old versions in historical evidence.
acceptance_test: Search current references for contradictory prepared/implemented claims on the same bounded task. Ensure a novice can tell what runs now and what remains unavailable without reading audit history.

observed_behavior: Backup serializes one learner snapshot, but afterward re-reads live state to populate completed-export counts. The backup screen permits navigation back while work runs, and ordinary learner writes are not fenced by backup export. Counts may describe records written after the archive snapshot.
expected_behavior: Record the exact snapshot that was exported and its coverage; later changes must not be described as backed up.
evidence: V2BackupEngine.writeStoreBackup obtains the first document; V2BackupCoordinator.createBackup obtains a second after output closes; V2BackupScreen onBack remains available. Static risk; concurrency execution was not performed.
proposed_correction: Use the written snapshot/manifest counts and coverage identity for ExportRecordEntity, or establish a documented consistent export boundary.
acceptance_test: Hold export after snapshot capture, navigate back and add an attempt/note, finish export. Recorded coverage must match archive bytes; post-snapshot work must remain visibly unexported.
